claims.text: Role in SSc: tocilizumab (anti-IL-6) preserves lung function in SSc-ILD; becoming an alt to mycophenolate, esp w predominant polyarthritis;
claims.quote: The anti-IL-6 blocker tocilizumab has been shown to preserve lung function in scleroderma-associated interstitial lung disease and is becoming an alternative to mycophenolate mofetil, especially if polyarthritis is a predominant feature

claims.text: rituximab is being evaluated for CTD-ILD and may have efficacy;
claims.quote: Rituximab is being evaluated for connective tissue disease–related interstitial lung disease and may have efficacy

claims.text: skin: tocilizumab and rituximab (among others) have shown modest benefit.
claims.quote: No definitive treatment has been shown to help with skin involvement. However, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, tocilizumab, rituximab, IV immune globulin, and cyclophosphamide all have shown modest benefit

claims.text: Tocilizumab (Actemra) dose, systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD): SSc-ILD: 162 mg once weekly SC.
claims.quote: The recommended dose of ACTEMRA for adult patients with SSc-ILD is 162 mg given once every week as a subcutaneous injection.
claims.locator: 2.4 Recommended Dosage for Systemic Sclerosis-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease

claims.text: Tocilizumab (Actemra) boxed warning: ↑ risk of serious infections that may lead to hospitalization or death; most pts were taking concomitant immunosuppressants such as methotrexate or corticosteroids.
claims.quote: Patients treated with ACTEMRA are at increased risk for developing serious infections that may lead to hospitalization or death [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1), Adverse Reactions (6.1)]. Most patients who developed these infections were taking concomitant immunosuppressants such as methotrexate or corticosteroids.

claims.text: Test for latent TB b4 ACTEMRA use and during therapy (except pts w COVID-19); start treatment for latent infection prior to ACTEMRA use.
claims.quote: Active tuberculosis, which may present with pulmonary or extrapulmonary disease. Patients, except those with COVID-19, should be tested for latent tuberculosis before ACTEMRA use and during therapy. Treatment for latent infection should be initiated prior to ACTEMRA use.

claims.text: Tocilizumab (Actemra) CI: known hypersensitivity to ACTEMRA.
claims.quote: ACTEMRA is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to ACTEMRA [see Warnings and Precautions (5.6)].

claims.text: Tocilizumab (Actemra) GI perforation: GI perforation reported, primarily as complications of diverticulitis; use w caution in pts who may be at ↑ risk; promptly evaluate fever, new onset abdominal Sx, and a change in bowel habits for early identification.
claims.quote: Events of gastrointestinal perforation have been reported in clinical trials, primarily as complications of diverticulitis in patients treated with ACTEMRA. Use ACTEMRA with caution in patients who may be at increased risk for gastrointestinal perforation. Promptly evaluate patients presenting with fever, new onset abdominal symptoms, and a change in bowel habits for early identification of gastrointestinal perforation [see Adverse Reactions (6.1)].

claims.text: Tocilizumab (Actemra) hepatotoxicity: Obtain liver test panel (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin) b4 ACTEMRA and every 4 to 8 wks for the first 6 mo, then every 3 mo; ⍉ initiate in RA, GCA or SSc-ILD pts w ALT or AST > 1.5× ULN; discontinue if ALT or AST > 5× ULN.
claims.quote: For RA, GCA and SSc-ILD patients, obtain a liver test panel (serum alanine aminotransferase [ALT], aspartate aminotransferase [AST], alkaline phosphatase, and total bilirubin) before initiating ACTEMRA, every 4 to 8 weeks after start of therapy for the first 6 months of treatment and every 3 months thereafter. It is not recommended to initiate ACTEMRA treatment in RA, GCA or SSc-ILD patients with elevated transaminases ALT or AST greater than 1.5× ULN. In patients who develop elevated ALT or AST greater than 5× ULN, discontinue ACTEMRA.

claims.text: Tocilizumab (Actemra) lab monitoring: ⍉ initiate in RA, GCA and SSc-ILD pts w ANC less than 2000 per mm3; if ANC less than 500 per mm3 treatment is not recommended.
claims.quote: It is not recommended to initiate ACTEMRA treatment in RA, GCA and SSc-ILD patients with a low neutrophil count, i.e., absolute neutrophil count (ANC) less than 2000 per mm3. In patients who develop an absolute neutrophil count less than 500 per mm3 treatment is not recommended.

claims.text: ⍉ initiate in RA, GCA and SSc-ILD pts w platelets below 100,000 per mm3; if platelets less than 50,000 per mm3 treatment is not recommended.
claims.quote: It is not recommended to initiate ACTEMRA treatment in RA, GCA and SSc-ILD patients with a platelet count below 100,000 per mm3. In patients who develop a platelet count less than 50,000 per mm3 treatment is not recommended.

claims.text: Assess lipid parameters approximately 4 to 8 wks following initiation of ACTEMRA.
claims.quote: Assess lipid parameters approximately 4 to 8 weeks following initiation of ACTEMRA therapy.

claims.text: Tocilizumab (Actemra) live vaccines: ⍉ use of live vaccines concurrently w ACTEMRA.
claims.quote: Avoid use of live vaccines concurrently with ACTEMRA as clinical safety has not been established.

claims.text: Tocilizumab (Actemra) CYP450 interaction: Inhibition of IL-6 signaling in RA pts treated w tocilizumab may restore CYP450 activities to higher levels than in the absence of tocilizumab, leading to ↑ metabolism of CYP450 substrate drugs.
claims.quote: Inhibition of IL-6 signaling in RA patients treated with tocilizumab may restore CYP450 activities to higher levels than those in the absence of tocilizumab leading to increased metabolism of drugs that are CYP450 substrates.

claims.text: On initiation or discontinuation of ACTEMRA, perform therapeutic monitoring of effect (e.g., warfarin) or drug concentration (e.g., cyclosporine or theophylline) and adjust the dose as needed.
claims.quote: Upon initiation or discontinuation of ACTEMRA, in patients being treated with these types of medicinal products, perform therapeutic monitoring of effect (e.g., warfarin) or drug concentration (e.g., cyclosporine or theophylline) and the individual dose of the medicinal product adjusted as needed.

claims.text: Rituximab (Rituxan) IV boxed warning — infusion reactions: Fatal infusion-related reactions w/in 24 h of RITUXAN infusion; approximately 80% of fatal reactions occurred w first infusion; monitor pts and discontinue RITUXAN infusion for severe reactions.
claims.quote: Fatal infusion-related reactions within 24 hours of RITUXAN infusion; approximately 80% of fatal reactions occurred with first infusion. Monitor patients and discontinue RITUXAN infusion for severe reactions (5.1).

claims.text: Rituximab (Rituxan) IV boxed warning — mucocutaneous reactions: Severe mucocutaneous reactions, some w fatal outcomes.
claims.quote: Severe mucocutaneous reactions, some with fatal outcomes (5.2).

claims.text: Rituximab (Rituxan) IV boxed warning — HBV reactivation: HBV reactivation, in some cases resulting in fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure, and death.
claims.quote: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation, in some cases resulting in fulminant hepatitis, hepatic failure, and death (5.3).

claims.text: Screen all pts for HBV infection b4 treatment initiation and monitor pts during and after treatment; discontinue RITUXAN and concomitant medications in the event of HBV reactivation.
claims.quote: Screen all patients for HBV infection before treatment initiation, and monitor patients during and after treatment with RITUXAN. Discontinue RITUXAN and concomitant medications in the event of HBV reactivation [see Warnings and Precautions (5.3)].

claims.text: Rituximab (Rituxan) IV boxed warning — PML: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) resulting in death.
claims.quote: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) resulting in death (5.4).

claims.text: Rituximab (Rituxan) IV infections: Serious, incl fatal, bacterial, fungal, and new or reactivated viral infections can occur during and following the completion of RITUXAN-based therapy.
claims.quote: Serious, including fatal, bacterial, fungal, and new or reactivated viral infections can occur during and following the completion of RITUXAN-based therapy.

claims.text: Discontinue RITUXAN for serious infections and institute appropriate anti-infective therapy.
claims.quote: Discontinue RITUXAN for serious infections and institute appropriate anti-infective therapy [see Adverse Reactions (6.1, 6.3)].

claims.text: Rituximab (Rituxan) IV cardiac reactions: Cardiac adverse reactions incl ventricular fibrillation, myocardial infarction, and cardiogenic shock may occur; discontinue infusions for serious or life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias; perform cardiac monitoring during and after all infusions in pts who develop clinically significant arrhythmias or who have a Hx of arrhythmia or angina.
claims.quote: Cardiac adverse reactions, including ventricular fibrillation, myocardial infarction, and cardiogenic shock may occur in patients receiving RITUXAN. Discontinue infusions for serious or life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias. Perform cardiac monitoring during and after all infusions of RITUXAN for patients who develop clinically significant arrhythmias, or who have a history of arrhythmia or angina

claims.text: Rituximab (Rituxan) IV live vaccines: Vaccination w live virus vaccines is not recommended b4 or during treatment; administer non live vaccines at least 4 wks prior to a course of RITUXAN.
claims.quote: The safety of immunization with live viral vaccines following RITUXAN therapy has not been studied and vaccination with live virus vaccines is not recommended before or during treatment. For patients treated with RITUXAN, physicians should review the patient's vaccination status and patients should, if possible, be brought up-to-date with all immunizations in agreement with current immunization guidelines prior to initiating RITUXAN and administer non live vaccines at least 4 weeks prior to a course of RITUXAN.

claims.text: Rituximab (Rituxan) IV premedication: Premedicate pts w an antihistamine and acetaminophen prior to dosing.
claims.quote: Premedicate patients with an antihistamine and acetaminophen prior to dosing.
